name: Bright Meridian: The Founding Century
description: Commissioned to mark the centennial of the GLMZ city charter, this four-hour holographic epic dramatizes the 'heroic founding' of the city's corponation governance structure, framing the dissolution of municipal government as a liberation rather than a corporate seizure. Produced by a consortium of seven corponations with Vantablack Media as distribution partner, the film features a cast of hundreds and was projected simultaneously in every licensed public space in M88 on the centennial date. Historian consultants later revealed their recommendations were systematically ignored.
cultural_impact: Paradoxically accelerated historical skepticism rather than dampening it — the film's aggressive triumphalism struck enough viewers as hollow that it became a reference point for how not to conduct corporate propaganda, studied in independent media criticism circles for years afterward.
story_hooks: One of the historian consultants kept copies of every recommendation that was rejected — and some of what they found in the archives has never been made public at all.
The simultaneous centennial projection was used to mask a city-wide data operation that no one noticed was happening; what was taken or planted is still unknown.
A minor character in the film — a 'heroic founding worker' — was based on a real person who was actually killed resisting the corporate takeover; their descendants want acknowledgment.
